A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same G2PM research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–B are readable and can be matched reliably despite table renumbering and page reflow.

before.justification: v1 reports original scaling experiments, architectural ablations, node and graph classification results, and cross-domain evaluations in Sections 3–5.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds link-prediction experiments in Section 4 and Table 3.

M1.justification: The random-walk tokenizer, Transformer encoder/decoder, EMA reconstruction targets, masked-substructure loss, augmentations, and downstream procedure are unchanged. Section 2.1 already described edge-level tokenization in v1; the added evaluation does not establish a method change.

E1.justification: v2 adds a dedicated link-prediction suite on Cora, Pubmed, and ogbl-collab. Cora and ogbl-collab are newly evaluated datasets, while Pubmed gains a task beyond its retained node-classification evaluation. This substantially extends task coverage; earlier benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: The new link-prediction comparison evaluates supervised GCN and GraphMAE against G2PM. GCN becomes an explicitly evaluated comparator, having previously appeared as a citation. Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: The added link-prediction experiment specifies an 80/5/15 training/validation/test split, Hit@20 for Cora and Pubmed, and Hit@50 for ogbl-collab. These are protocols for the new evaluation; existing splits, probing and fine-tuning procedures, and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The architectural and training ablations in Table 1 and Figure 5, convergence analysis in Figure 6, receptive-field analysis in Figure 7, and cross-domain analyses are retained unchanged. No additional ablation, robustness test, or case study accompanies the new benchmark results.

E5.justification: Appendix B.2 states five runs with different random seeds in both versions. The new table follows the existing plus/minus reporting practice; no new uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence interval, or significance test is introduced.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds substantive results for link prediction: G2PM reports 90.4 ± 0.8 and 88.0 ± 3.8 Hit@20 on Cora and Pubmed, and 47.1 ± 0.6 Hit@50 on ogbl-collab. Its reported means exceed both new-table comparators across all three datasets. This adds a task-level empirical finding; numerical results and plotted findings in the retained experiments are unchanged.

T1.justification: The graph and random-walk definitions and Equations 1–7 are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, derivation, or formal assumption is added, and Appendix A retains the same substructure-dependency discussion.

C1.justification: The abstract extends its empirical outperformance claim to link-level tasks. It also explicitly mentions cross-graph pretraining, which was already evaluated in v1 Section 5. The central claims about message-passing-free modeling, scalability, and transferable substructure representations remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The new link-prediction discussion tentatively attributes G2PM's performance to substructures capturing latent connectivity patterns, and GraphMAE's advantage over GCN to unlabeled-data pretraining. Existing interpretations and future directions remain; removing the conclusion's 'Limitation and Future Works' lead-in does not remove its substantive content.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the same hardware, software versions, optimizer settings, hyperparameters, and tuning ranges. Code/data access information is unchanged. The added link evaluation supplies split and metric information but no accompanying implementation or dataset-specific tuning details.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds five cited works, including G2PT, Pure Transformers Are Powerful Graph Learners, Revisiting Random Walks for Learning on Graphs, and two graph-generation papers. These extend the citation coverage without substantially rewriting the research positioning or introducing corresponding baseline experiments.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited abstract and grammar edits, inserts the link-prediction paragraph, identifies the corresponding author, and adds acknowledgements. Section organization and most prose remain intact, including both appendices.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 3 beside the link-prediction discussion, causing nearby text to reflow and later tables to be renumbered. It also adds conference-footer formatting. The seven existing figures retain identical embedded content, and retained tables keep their substantive display structure.

improvement.justification: The added link-prediction comparisons provide empirical support for the edge-level applicability already described in v1, and the related-work additions improve coverage. These are useful but bounded gains: the core method and earlier evidence are unchanged, and the new experiment lacks accompanying link-specific implementation details in Appendix B.
